key_features: C3 wearable sync in the Juniper app (Apple, Fitbit, Garmin) covering activity, heart rate and blood glucose; C4 practitioner-led adaptive weight programs with unlimited follow-up consults; Bluetooth digital scale shipped with first delivery; manual weight and waist tracking with progress graphs; 550,000+ patients across brands, 100,000+ Juniper members in Australia
why_fit: Tier A. Everything except body composition is already connected: wearables in, scale in, waist measured by hand. A 2-photo scan replaces the tape measure and turns waist and composition into a tracked series the clinical team can review.

key_features: C3 wearable and platform sync (Apple Watch, Garmin, Fitbit, Google Fit); C4 personalised guidance and insights generated from the user's own data; 14-day CGM sensors with live glucose view; meal, movement, sleep and stress logging; 70+ blood markers and biological age; dietitian and nurse support; 30,000+ members
why_fit: Tier A. Densest consumer data loop in Australia (glucose plus wearables plus food) with no body-composition input. Fat mass versus lean mass is the metric its metabolic-health story is missing.

size: not disclosed (180+ active clinicians, 1,850+ partner locations)
key_features: C3 30+ wearable device integrations; C4 AI-supported continuous care with personalised programs and longitudinal view; 100+ biomarkers, full-body MRI, bone density, CGM, VO2 max and genetic testing; consumer plans from $299 plus enterprise executive health (BCG, BHP, Bain); 20,000+ patients; AU$65M Series A in 2026
why_fit: Tier A. Sells longitudinal body data as the product and already pays facility cost for clinical body composition (DEXA, bone density). A phone scan supplies between-visit composition tracking at near-zero marginal cost.

key_features: C3 Apple Health and Google Fit sync for workouts, meditations and mindful minutes; C4 Centr Coach personalised training plans across five goal tracks; nutritionist-approved meal plans with macros, shopping lists and dietary variants; connected equipment line
why_fit: Tier A on features, flagged on geography. Multi-pillar app in the Erakulis shape (train, eat, recover) with a celebrity-led brand and no body measurement anywhere in the loop. Confirm the current head office before outreach.

company_name: Digital Wellness (CSIRO Total Wellbeing Diet Online)
size: not disclosed (offices in Sydney, New York and London)
key_features: C3 activity tracking with smartwatch integration; C4 AI-inspired weight-loss coach (Hope) plus personalised higher-protein low-GI meal plans; online food tracker and weight tracker with real-time results; optional human health coaches; member community; 500,000+ people through the program since 2014
why_fit: Tier A. Commercial licensee of the CSIRO program, so the target is the operator rather than the public research agency. Scale weight is the entire progress story today; composition separates fat loss from day-to-day weight noise.

key_features: C3 wearable sync driving member rewards and milestones; C4 AI-powered tools funded by the 2026 Series A; white-label branded member app, multi-site and franchise management, marketing automation, reporting; brands include Fitstop, KX Pilates, Strong Pilates, VAURA, Gold's Gym and UFC Gym; 1M+ members across 10+ countries
why_fit: Tier A and the widest-reach single integration on this list: one build would put a body scan inside the member apps of many Australian fitness brands at once, sold as a platform feature rather than app by app.

key_features: C3 device and app links (Fitbit, Garmin, Apple Health, Google Fit, Strava, Polar, Suunto, Misfit) awarding points on steps, workouts, heart rate, mindful minutes and sleep; C4 personalised program with in-app and face-to-face health assessments plus a Vitality Age calculator; rewards, partner discounts and premium benefits
why_fit: Tier A. Already pays members for verified activity data and runs recurring health assessments. Body composition is the assessment input it cannot collect remotely today.

hq_city: Sydney, NSW (head office now listed in New York)
key_features: C3 Apple Health support in the member app; C4 AI and behavioural-science algorithms that personalise engagement per member; gamified adherence with streaks, leaderboards and gift-card rewards, SMS and push reminders; sells to health plans, Managed Medicaid, government agencies and workers' compensation; HIPAA and SOC 2 Type 2 attested
why_fit: Tier A on features and the strongest compliance posture in the set. A pure engagement engine with no body metric; a scan gives its payer customers an objective outcome measure alongside adherence. Flag: Sydney origin, New York head office.

key_features: C3 first-party wearables (VECTOR PRO, VECTOR CORE, CATAPULT ONE) plus PERCH weight-room sensing; C4 AI-supported performance, load and injury-risk analytics; video and tactical analysis, scouting tools; 5,500+ elite teams across 40+ sports in 128 countries
why_fit: Tier A. Owns the athlete-monitoring data layer for elite and academy sport and has no body-composition input; a phone scan fits squads and pathway programs that cannot access DEXA.

key_features: C3 first-party medical-grade wearable sensors (ViMove+ movement sensors, ViSafe+ workplace sensors); C4 Video AI movement analysis from camera alone (running gait, upper and lower limb) plus a research algorithm library; clinical, elite sport and workplace safety customers
why_fit: Tier A. Already sells objective human measurement from cameras and sensors, so a phone-camera body-composition module extends the same buyer conversation (clinicians, teams, employers) rather than starting a new one.

company_name: Sweat (The Bikini Body Training Company Pty Ltd)
key_features: C3 Apple Health and Apple Watch integration; 70+ programs and thousands of workouts, 500+ recipes, in-app progress tracking, home and gym variants; 39M+ downloads; repurchased by its founders from iFIT in 2023, so Australian-owned again
why_fit: Tier B, top of it. Largest Australian-owned consumer fitness app, selling a body-transformation outcome evidenced only by workout logs and user photos. Adaptive AI coaching is not documented, so this is a product-expansion pitch to product and growth owners.

key_features: 1,000+ classes (Pilates, strength, running, yoga, HIIT, mobility), 100+ mindset and breathwork sessions, 1,000+ dietitian-approved recipes, 20+ guided programs, in-app run and walk mapping, community challenges, pre and postnatal content; 2.8M community, 1M+ downloads, 4.8 App Store rating; Melbourne studio and retail range
why_fit: Tier B. The Australian consumer app closest in shape to Erakulis (move, eat, mind in one loop) with no wearable integration or body metric documented. A scan is both the missing measurement and a credible premium-tier hook.

key_features: C3 Apple Health integration; daily 28-minute home workouts (HIIT, cardio, strength, yoga, Pilates), 7-day customisable meal plans with swap, drop and scale options, mindfulness and meditation, in-app progress tracking, 64,000+ member community, menopause, pregnancy and postnatal programs; 500,000+ people through the program
why_fit: Tier B. Built on defined transformation windows (28 days, 8-week challenges), which is exactly the cadence a repeatable scan is designed to measure.

key_features: C3 HealthKit logging of workouts and meditations; 600+ workouts across 8 programs, 5 new workouts weekly, 500+ dietitian-approved recipes with meal plans and shopping lists, 130+ pregnancy-safe workouts and postpartum programs; $10 to $20 AUD per month with a 2-week trial
why_fit: Tier B. Women's transformation subscription with pre and postnatal cohorts, where body change is the entire value proposition and self-measurement is least reliable.

key_features: 12-week transformation rounds with tailored and express workouts, 1,300+ recipes with shopping-list integration, mindset video lessons, in-app tracker, menopause program; iOS and Android; running in Australia for over a decade
why_fit: Tier B. The original Australian 12-week body-transformation program. Every round opens and closes on a before-and-after that is currently evidenced by photos and scale weight only.

company_name: Transform by Fitaz (FitazFK Health Pty Ltd)
key_features: 200+ at-home workouts of 18 to 28 minutes, 800+ recipes, staged programs (weight-loss reset, strength and tone, shape and sculpt) plus pregnancy, postpartum, perimenopause and Pilates tracks, expert community, results-in-8-weeks promise with money-back guarantee; 200,000+ members globally
why_fit: Tier B. Sells an 8-week result under a money-back guarantee, so objective before-and-after measurement is tied directly to its refund exposure and marketing claims. No wearable or AI features documented.

key_features: 12-week program app with 18 meal plans (keto, vegetarian, 5:2 variants), 700+ recipes, daily guided workouts, regular health tracking, mindfulness and meditation audio, member community and ongoing support; 80,000+ members; Australian and UK operations
why_fit: Tier B. Rapid-weight-loss program where lean-mass preservation is the credibility question, and composition tracking is the direct answer to it. GDPR applies through the UK operation.

key_features: 12-week doctor-led low-carb program by app and web: weekly unlocked lessons, weekly meal plans, 450+ recipes, blood-glucose and habit progress tracking, optional one-to-one dietitian telehealth, HbA1c test referrals, community support; 9,500+ members; Diabetes Australia partnership; published 12-month outcomes study
why_fit: Tier B. Clinical-adjacent metabolic program already tracking glucose and habits. Body composition adds the visible-change metric that carries members through a 12-week course and strengthens its outcomes reporting.

key_features: C4 adaptive resistance adjusting load in real time to the user's movement (7kg to 180kg digital weight, algorithmic control up to 40 times per second); Trainer+ hardware with app, 200+ exercises, 300+ classes, performance logging, time-under-tension and eccentric modes; $51.4M raised across 4 rounds; US and EU markets
why_fit: Tier B. The purest adaptive-AI training product in Australia and already data-native at rep level, yet body composition is the outcome its performance data cannot produce. Note: the main website was in a pre-launch holding state when checked, so verify commercial status first.

size: 51-200 employees (source-dependent: approx. 51 in Jun 2025, LinkedIn band 51-200); revenue $54.3M (2026); 4,000+ teams and organisations
key_features: Human-measurement systems: ForceDecks force plates, NordBord, ForceFrame, HumanTrak 3D movement analysis, SmartSpeed, SmartJump, AirBands, plus TeleHab and MoveHealth exercise-prescription apps; customers across elite sport, universities, defence and clinics; 1,100sqm global head office in Brisbane
why_fit: Tier B on feature count and Tier A on intent: it already sells objective human measurement to exactly the buyers who would resell body composition. Treat as a partnership or OEM motion rather than an in-app feature sale.

key_features: C3 activity trackers and wearables linked for team movement challenges and leaderboard points; custom corporate wellbeing platform with monthly campaigns, wellbeing assessments, private personal health charting, workouts, meditations and recipes, social wall and recognition, employer reporting; iOS and Android
why_fit: Tier B. Employer platform already ingesting wearable data and running assessments, where a remote body-composition check would make challenge outcomes measurable instead of step-count only.

key_features: Digital sleep screening, assessment and triage into personalised pathways, plus education and habit programs; sold to employers, insurers and health and wellbeing providers; offered as an HCF member benefit; Virgin Pulse certified partner; ISO 27001 certified
why_fit: Tier B. Owns the recovery pillar of the Erakulis loop and sells into Australian employers and insurers with a security posture that clears procurement. Body data would be a new pillar for them, so approach as a partnership.

key_features: C3 member app using HealthKit to share activity and workout data and to drive activity incentives; FWD, a personalised fitness and nutrition app extending the brand beyond clubs; Fernwood Pulse at-home access included with membership; milestone tracking, bookings and member perks
why_fit: Tier B and a deliberate exception to the gym-chain exclusion, because the digital layer is real (own app plus the FWD product). Women-only network with in-club touchpoints where a first scan is easy to introduce and then repeated at home.

key_features: Member app for workout tracking, class booking, progress and community; performance-based session blocks (Lift, Perform, Condition, Sweat) with nutrition support and coach-led programming; runs on the Hapana platform for its international growth
why_fit: Tier B. A performance-benchmark franchise whose members already retest strength and conditioning, so a periodic body-composition retest fits an existing habit. No wearable integration documented.

key_features: Easy Diet Diary consumer app: food logging with barcode scanning against the Australian food database, exercise tracking, macro and micronutrient monitoring, energy in kilojoules or calories, progress charts, sharing with practitioners via FoodWorks.online; FoodWorks Professional used by hospitals, private practices, universities and food manufacturers; 15,000+ five-star reviews
why_fit: Tier B. Australia's default nutrition-data company and the local counterpart to the food-scanning side of the Erakulis stack. Logging is barcode and manual rather than photo AI, and there is no body metric, so both gaps are open.

size: not disclosed (A$40M raised; clients include Woolworths, McDonald's, KPMG, Bupa)

why_fit: Tier B and the weakest feature match here (no wearable or body-data layer documented), kept because it is a large Australian employee-care platform with a preventive-health roadmap and enterprise procurement already solved.
